explanations: terra: The waiting period of three قُرُوءٍ uses the ق ر ء family named by the section, while the same ayah forbids women to hide what Allah has created in their wombs; reproductive time, uterine enclosure, and divine creation meet directly.

luna: The source section’s ر ب ب dictionary form is “to rear a child”; this ayah gives that growth a concrete duration by naming mothers’ nursing for two complete years. | terra: Two complete years of nursing are set for one who wishes to complete suckling, while the father bears provision; early bodily growth is given a measured duration and sustained by parental care.
terra: Bones are raised and clothed with flesh before the observer sees that Allah is powerful over all things; bodily reassembly mirrors prenatal building while proving resurrection.

terra: Old age reaches the owner of a fruitful garden while his children are weak, and fire destroys the garden; aged body, dependent offspring, vegetation, and perishing provision meet in one warning.

luna: The section hears creation and proportioning as bodily formation; this ayah directly says God forms people in the wombs however He wills. | terra: هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُصَوِّرُكُمْ فِى ٱلْأَرْحَامِ كَيْفَ يَشَآءُ locates divinely willed bodily form inside the womb, clarifying what the section means by the fetus acquiring its shape.

terra: Love of women, sons, livestock, and cultivated land is presented together as the enjoyment of worldly life; reproduction, offspring, pasture, and dunya meet within one inventory of transient attachment.
terra: The wife of Imran dedicates what is in her womb to her Lord, placing the still-hidden child within divine nurture before the delivery and growth narrated in 3:36-37.

terra: At delivery the mother identifies the child as female, names her Mary, and entrusts her offspring to Allah; the hidden womb of 3:35 becomes a born and sexed child whom 3:37 then causes to grow.

terra: Mary's Lord accepts her and أَنۢبَتَهَا نَبَاتًا حَسَنًا, causing her to grow as a good growth under care; divine nurture of a child is expressed through the plant image that the section pairs with bodily growth.

luna: Zakariya likewise asks how he can have a boy when old age has reached him and his wife is barren, making conception at the far end of life a reversal. | terra: Zechariah asks how he can have a boy when بَلَغَنِىَ ٱلْكِبَرُ and his wife is barren; old age and new gestation meet as a divinely crossed bodily boundary.
terra: Mary asks how she can have a child when no man has touched her, and the answer is that Allah creates what He wills; the ayah marks divine creation beyond the ordinary sperm-to-womb route.
terra: Jesus is likened to Adam, whom Allah created from dust and commanded to be; this gives the section's gestational sequence a clear exception without weakening divine authorship of form.
terra: Creation from a single soul, its mate, and the dispersal of many men and women frames individual gestation within the multiplication of one human family and explicitly invokes womb-ties.
terra: Orphans are tested until marriageable age and the appearance of sound judgment, making growth into adult capacity a practical threshold rather than an undifferentiated span.
terra: The statement that the human was created weak supplies the vulnerable bodily condition from which the section's growth toward soundness and strength proceeds.

luna: This ayah joins human creation from clay to an appointed term, a specific link between the section’s bodily origin and its measured life course. | terra: Creation from clay is followed by a decreed term and another term known to Allah, linking bodily origin to measured duration even though prenatal stages are not shown.

luna: The section’s womb sequence may connect with this ayah’s “resting place and deposit,” which some readings associate with womb and repository; the ayah itself does not specify those locations, so the parallel is uncertain. | terra: Humanity is produced from a single soul and given a place of settlement and deposit; these have been read in bodily and womb-related ways, but the ayah itself leaves the locations unstated, so the uterine connection remains uncertain.

luna: The section reads creation and proportioning bodily; this ayah says God created humans and then formed them, a direct human-form parallel. | terra: Allah says He created and then shaped humankind before the command concerning Adam, presenting bodily form as a distinct completion within creation.

luna: The section follows human formation as a life stage; this ayah describes a spouse bearing a light burden that later grows heavier, a concrete pregnancy progression. | terra: A light pregnancy becomes heavy before the parents ask for a sound child, presenting gestation as gradual bodily accumulation and completion within the single-soul creation story.
terra: Allah begins creation and repeats it before the return of all, a concise statement of the relation made bodily and evidential in 75:37-40.

luna: This ayah repeats the section’s growth-and-decay image: rain adorns the land with plants, then they are harvested and vanish, making visible what passes. | terra: The likeness of worldly life joins rain, earth's growth, human and animal food, full adornment, and sudden cutting down; it illuminates the section's move from formed body to transient pasture.
terra: Humans are produced from earth and caused to dwell and flourish in it; the earthly origin and cultivation verb support the section's meeting of formed body and growing ground.
terra: Sarah's amazement joins her own old age to an aged husband at the announcement of a child, placing birth at the far end of the ordinary life sequence.
terra: When Joseph reaches full strength, Allah gives him judgment and knowledge; it is a repeated formulation of mature bodily arrival, though without 28:14's additional word for full development.

luna: The section’s ق د ر root means setting things to a measure; this ayah joins what wombs decrease or increase to the claim that all things are with God by measure. | terra: Allah knows what every female bears, what wombs diminish or increase, and declares that everything with Him has a measure; this joins the hidden womb to the section's قدّر as exact apportioning.
terra: Those who prefer worldly life over the Hereafter and turn others from Allah's way enact the same preference named in 87:16, here joined to active distortion of guidance.
terra: Abraham praises Allah for granting Ishmael and Isaac عَلَى ٱلْكِبَرِ; offspring arriving in old age makes the section's two distant bodily stages coincide.

terra: Everything's treasuries belong to Allah and it is sent down only in a known measure; without specifying the body, the ayah gives provision the same exact apportioning that governs gestation in the section.

luna: The section’s formed-body image connects to the preceding announcement of a human being created from clay; the next ayah gives the forming and spirit-breathing detail. | terra: Allah announces that He is creating a human from clay, supplying the bodily referent that 15:29 then proportions and breathes into.

luna: The section’s creation-and-proportioning image meets this account of the human being formed and given spirit; the body is explicitly the object of the making. | terra: The command follows فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُۥ وَنَفَخْتُ فِيهِ مِن رُّوحِى; bodily proportioning precedes animation, clarifying سوى as preparation of a formed human body.
terra: Abraham asks whether he is being given good news عَلَىٰٓ أَن مَّسَّنِىَ ٱلْكِبَرُ, explicitly making old age the apparent boundary challenged by the promised birth.
terra: Human creation from a sperm-drop is immediately set against the resulting person's open disputation; the fully articulate adversary is traced back to a minute bodily beginning.

luna: The section’s ك ب ر branch names old age; this ayah says some are returned to the most decrepit age, reversing their earlier knowledge and strength. | terra: Allah creates and causes death, and some are returned to the most abject age until knowledge is lost; bodily and mental decline follow the section's stage of maturity.

luna: This ayah begins after birth, when people are brought from their mothers’ wombs, and names the faculties given as they enter life beyond the section’s prenatal stages. | terra: Allah brings humans from their mothers' wombs knowing nothing and gives hearing, sight, and hearts, marking the passage from enclosed fetus to equipped living person.
terra: These people prefer worldly life over the Hereafter, a repeated formulation of the choice in 87:16-17 and the ethical outcome of the bodily lifetime traced by the section.

luna: The section’s ك ب ر dictionary sense is old age; this ayah names parents reaching old age while dependent on the child they raised. | terra: إِمَّا يَبْلُغَنَّ عِندَكَ ٱلْكِبَرَ places one or both parents in old age under the grown child's care, making the ك ب ر family's bodily life-stage sense ethically concrete.

luna: The source section’s ر ب ب dictionary branch is child-rearing; this prayer names parents’ having raised the speaker when small, giving that lexical sense a human scene. | terra: The prayer كَمَا رَبَّيَانِى صَغِيرًا uses the ر ب ب family for parents raising a small child; beside 17:23's aged parents, nurture and decline become the two ends of one life cycle.
terra: The question about becoming bones and fragments and then being raised as a new creation makes bodily decomposition the apparent obstacle.
terra: The answer to 17:49 is that the One who originated them the first time will return them, using first bodily creation as the decisive comparison.
terra: The Creator of the heavens and earth is able to create the like of the objectors and has appointed their term, combining re-creative power with a measured lifespan.
terra: The garden owner doubts the Hour and assumes a favorable return; 18:37 answers with his dust-and-drop origin, so denial of return is exposed by the ordered body he inhabits.

luna: The section treats creation and proportioning as bodily life stages; the speaker recalls being made from earth, then a drop, then formed as a man. | terra: The garden owner's companion recalls creation from dust, then a drop, then ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰكَ رَجُلًا; bodily formation is the argument against self-secure confidence in the garden.

terra: The garden's produce is encompassed and its owner wrings his hands over the ruined trellises; it realizes the destruction that stands between 18:37's formed man and 18:45's withered-world image.

luna: The section explicitly joins the formed body to a drying pasture as two sides of one warning; this ayah depicts worldly life as watered growth that becomes scattered dry matter. | terra: Worldly life is water-grown vegetation that mingles, then becomes dry fragments scattered by wind; it is the exact withering-garden counterpart to the ordered body in 18:37.

luna: After the garden and dry-growth image in 18:45, this ayah distinguishes the passing adornments of worldly life from good deeds that remain. | terra: Wealth and children are called the adornment of worldly life immediately after 18:45's withering vegetation; human offspring are thus named within the garden image paired with the formed man of 18:37.

luna: The section’s ك ب ر branch names aging; Zakariya describes weakened bones and gray hair while asking for a child, bringing old age and new life together. | terra: Zechariah describes weakened bones and a head aflame with grey hair while asking for an heir; bodily signs of decline precede the promised child's beginning.
luna: This continues Zakariya’s old-age prayer from 19:4: he names his fear about those after him and his barren wife, giving the request for a child its bodily boundary.

luna: Zakariya says his wife is barren and he has reached extreme old age, a specific boundary to the section’s sequence from womb to aged body. | terra: His wife is barren and he has reached مِنَ ٱلْكِبَرِ عِتِيًّا, so the possibility of a child is placed beyond ordinary reproductive ageing.
terra: The answer recalls that the Lord created Zechariah before when he was nothing; first creation answers the old man's doubt about a new birth, just as it answers doubt about resurrection.
terra: Mary names the absence of male contact and unchastity, defining the ordinary reproductive condition that this conception will cross.
terra: The promised boy is made a sign and mercy and the matter is decreed; bodily creation without the ordinary father is presented as an intentional boundary case, not an accident.
terra: Mary conceives and withdraws to a distant place, restoring a real pregnancy and enclosed bodily development after the exceptional conception.
terra: Labor pains drive Mary to the palm trunk, giving the approach and crisis of birth the concrete bodily scene suggested by the section's secondary sense of nearness to delivery.
terra: The human asks whether, after dying, he will be brought out alive; the doubt focuses directly on continuity of the body across death.
terra: The answer recalls that Allah created the person before when he was nothing, making initial creation the precedent for renewed life.
terra: The infant Moses is carried by the water under divine protection and is to be formed under Allah's eye; the child is both physically preserved and deliberately brought through an early stage.

luna: The section joins creating, proportioning, measuring, and guiding into a human-life image; Moses gives a parallel formula: God gave each thing its creation, then guided it. | terra: رَبُّنَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَعْطَىٰ كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلْقَهُۥ ثُمَّ هَدَىٰ joins Lord, each thing's fitted creation, and guidance, closely restating the logic of 87:1-3 that the section applies to the body.
terra: From earth humans are created, into it returned, and from it brought out again, joining bodily origin, death, and renewed emergence in the same ground on which vegetation grows.
terra: The offender who comes to his Lord faces hell where he neither dies nor lives, exactly repeating the bodily boundary between death and life stated in 87:13 and showing its punitive sense.
terra: The chaste woman receives the breathed spirit and she and her son become a sign; womb-bearing is retained while ordinary generation is exceeded.
terra: كَمَا بَدَأْنَآ أَوَّلَ خَلْقٍۢ نُّعِيدُهُۥ promises to repeat creation as it began, turning the section's first bodily formation into a pattern for the end.

terra: The Hour makes every nursing mother neglect her infant and every pregnant female cast off her burden; ordinary nurture and gestational completion are violently interrupted, defining the bodily order's catastrophic boundary.

luna: The section’s formed/unformed fetus and old-age stages meet here in مخلقة وغير مخلقة and أرذل العمر; the same ayah sets bodily formation beside dead earth swelling back to life. | terra: This ayah gathers the section's whole bodily arc: dust, sperm, clot, a formed or unformed lump, settlement in wombs to a fixed term, childhood, maturity, death or decrepit age; its closing revival of dead earth also places body and pasture in one scene.
luna: After the fetus and revived earth in 22:5, this ayah states that God gives life to the dead; it makes the preceding bodily and soil images an argument for resurrection.
luna: This ayah follows 22:5’s bodily stages by naming the coming Hour and resurrection from graves, the judgment that the prior life-and-earth images support.

luna: This opens the same account whose next verses trace the womb stages: human creation begins from an extract of clay, before descendants enter the secure lodging of 23:13. | terra: Human creation begins from an extract of clay, supplying the earthly starting material for 23:13-14's womb and bodily transformations.

luna: This ayah places the human drop in a secure lodging until an appointed term, giving a concrete prenatal interval for the section’s body stages. | terra: The drop is placed فِى قَرَارٍۢ مَّكِينٍۢ, a secure lodging that concretizes the womb closing around and holding the developing child; 23:14 supplies the transformations within it.

luna: The section distinguishes a fully formed from an unformed mudghah; 23:14 lays out the body’s progression through clot, tissue, bones, and flesh before another creation. | terra: The drop becomes clot, lump, bones, and clothed flesh before being produced as another creation; it expands the section's خلق and سوى into a bodily sequence, continuing 23:13's secure womb.

luna: After the developmental sequence in 23:12–14, this ayah says people die, extending the section’s body-through-life arc to its end. | terra: After the ordered prenatal sequence, the human must die; this gives bodily completion its temporal boundary.

luna: This next ayah says people are raised after death, completing the life-cycle sequence begun with bodily formation in 23:12. | terra: After death comes resurrection, completing the creation–death–re-creation arc begun in 23:12-14.

terra: Water is sent down in measure and lodged in the earth, a deliberate structural parallel to reproductive fluid lodged in a secure womb; here the measured deposit sustains the growing ground and can also be withdrawn.
terra: Hearing, sight, and hearts are attributed to the One who produced humankind; within the surah that narrated fetal formation in 23:12-14, these faculties show what that formed body becomes.
terra: The question whether humans thought they were created aimlessly and would not be returned states explicitly the purpose-and-resurrection claim implicit in the section's ordered body.
terra: Children who reach puberty move to the adult rule of seeking permission, making bodily maturation a definite threshold in the life course.
terra: Elderly women beyond expectation of marriage occupy a stated reproductive and social boundary, complementing the section's movement from bodily maturity into old age.
terra: Allah creates everything and فَقَدَّرَهُۥ تَقْدِيرًا, an exact formulation of the section's definition of placing each thing in its particular measure and form.
terra: Allah creates the human from water and then establishes ties of blood and marriage, extending bodily origin into generational kinship.

luna: The source section cites ر ب ب in the sense of raising a child; Pharaoh uses the matching verb نربك for having reared Moses as a child. | terra: Pharaoh asks Moses أَلَمْ نُرَبِّكَ فِينَا وَلِيدًا, using the ر ب ب family for a human ruler's claim to have raised an infant; it clarifies the nurture sense while contrasting human patronage with the true Lord.
terra: The question asks who begins creation and then repeats it; in its provision context, renewed creation belongs to the same ordering power that sustains embodied life.
terra: Moses' mother is told to nurse her newborn and promised his return, adding the vulnerable nourishment immediately after birth to the section's account of a child being raised stage by stage.

luna: The section cites س و ي in the dictionary sense of a man reaching the end of youth; this ayah uses واستوى of Moses after he reaches maturity. | terra: بَلَغَ أَشُدَّهُۥ وَٱسْتَوَىٰ uses the سوى family at the arrival of full strength and maturity, exactly matching the section's secondary dictionary sense of completed youth.
terra: The addressees are asked to see how Allah begins creation and then repeats it, stating the same first-formation argument that the section draws from the fetus.
terra: Travel through the earth is commanded to inspect how creation began, after which Allah produces the final creation; bodily return is placed within observable created origins.
luna: This ayah calls worldly life play and amusement and the home of the Hereafter the real life, sharpening the section’s contrast between the present and lasting life.
terra: The summons to reflect within themselves leads to creation in truth and for a named term; it turns embodied self-knowledge into recognition that created life has a limit and purpose.
terra: Allah begins creation, repeats it, and then humans are returned to Him, extending the body's measured beginning to its final destination.
terra: Originating and repeating creation are attributed to Allah, and repetition is described as easier; the ayah generalizes the fetus-to-resurrection inference.
terra: Revived earth is offered as evidence that the same giver of life revives the dead and is powerful over everything; pasture, resurrection, and the power sense of ق د ر meet directly.

luna: The section’s س و ي branch names the body at its youthful peak and its ك ب ر branch old age; this ayah explicitly reverses strength into weakness and gray hair. | terra: Human life is explicitly ordered as weakness, strength, then weakness and grey hair; the second weakness reverses bodily completion and gives the section's maturation-to-old-age arc its clearest formulation.

luna: The section’s body-in-formation continues into maternal bearing and nursing here; the ayah names pregnancy’s weakness and two years of weaning. | terra: The mother carries the child in weakness upon weakness and weans in two years, adding maternal bodily cost and early nurture to the section's prenatal-to-childhood sequence.
terra: Knowledge of what is in the wombs belongs to Allah, emphasizing the hiddenness of the very formation that the section unfolds through word families.

luna: This precedes the section-cited 32:9 account: it says God perfected everything He created, introducing the human formation and spirit passage in 32:8–9. | terra: Allah perfects everything He creates and begins human creation from clay; 32:8-9 narrow that general perfection into reproductive fluid and the proportioned body.

luna: The section’s bodily course begins before birth; this ayah names human descendants as coming from an extract of fluid, leading into the proportioning in 32:9. | terra: Human progeny is made from an extract of lowly fluid; it supplies the reproductive material that 32:9 then proportions and animates.

luna: The section cites this ayah’s سواه and breathing of spirit as a bodily creation parallel to the womb-shaped person. | terra: ثُمَّ سَوَّىٰهُۥ joins bodily proportioning to the breath of spirit and the gift of hearing, sight, and hearts; the ordered body becomes a living, perceiving human.
terra: The objection asks whether, once lost in earth, humans can be in a new creation; beside 32:7-9's first bodily formation, it exposes the disbelief that the earlier sequence answers.

luna: The section’s measured-body image meets an ayah that names pregnancy, delivery, and allotted lifetimes, with each lifespan recorded. | terra: Creation from dust and then a drop is joined to pairing, every conception and birth under Allah's knowledge, and every extended or shortened life recorded; formation and measured lifespan are one act.

luna: This ayah makes aging a reversal of creation: whoever is granted long life is turned back in form, matching the section’s movement from bodily completion toward decline. | terra: Whomever Allah grants long life He reverses فِى ٱلْخَلْقِ, so ageing is presented as an undoing within creation itself, a direct counter-motion to bodily completion.

luna: The section’s body begins in the womb; this passage begins its resurrection argument by reminding the denier that he was created from a drop. | terra: The human created from a sperm-drop becomes an open opponent, setting developed agency against its fragile origin before the bone-and-resurrection dispute.

luna: After the human origin in 36:77, this ayah asks who can revive decayed bones, making the body’s later state the question answered by 36:79. | terra: The disputant forgets his own creation and asks who can revive decayed bones; the section's formed body becomes the forgotten premise of his objection.

luna: This ayah answers 36:78 that the One who produced the body the first time can revive it, the same creation-to-resurrection inference the section draws from 75:37–40. | terra: The answer is that the One who produced the bones the first time will revive them, explicitly making initial bodily formation the measure of re-creation.
terra: The Creator of the heavens and earth is asked whether He is able to create the like of decomposed humans; the affirmative answer joins divine power to bodily re-creation.

luna: This introduces the human creation sequence completed in 38:72, where proportioning and spirit-breathing make the bodily link explicit. | terra: Allah announces creation of a human from clay; 38:72 contributes the subsequent proportioning and animation, so this ayah states the material beginning of that formed body.

luna: This ayah likewise follows the human form being proportioned by the breathing of spirit, adding the embodied creation sequence that the section cites at 32:9. | terra: The repeated formula of proportioning the clay human and breathing spirit makes the completed form the threshold between fashioned body and living person.

luna: The section traces formation inside the womb; 39:6 locates creation after creation in mothers’ wombs within three darknesses. | terra: The fetus is made خَلْقًا مِّنۢ بَعْدِ خَلْقٍۢ inside three darknesses, making the section's gathering, stage-by-stage formation, and enclosing womb visible.

luna: The section’s drying-pasture comparison recurs here as rain-fed growth that yellows and becomes debris, a second image of created life’s fading. | terra: Rain is conducted through earth, crops vary in color, then yellow and crumble; the visible sequence supplies a vegetal analogue for the body's measured growth and decline.

luna: This ayah says God shaped people and made their forms good, a concrete bodily use of the section’s formation roots. | terra: وَصَوَّرَكُمْ فَأَحْسَنَ صُوَرَكُمْ links good bodily form, provision, and Allah as Lord, reinforcing the section's sound-body and nurturing-Rabb senses together.

luna: This ayah follows human life from dust and drop through infancy and maturity to old age, the same bodily course the section hears in the surah’s roots. | terra: Dust, sperm, clot, emergence as a child, full strength, old age, death, and an appointed term are set in one ayah, matching the section's reading of the surah's word families as an entire human lifespan.

luna: After 40:67’s infancy-to-old-age sequence, this ayah says God gives life and causes death, extending that bodily chronology to its limit. | terra: After 40:67's complete sequence of bodily ages, هُوَ ٱلَّذِى يُحْىِۦ وَيُمِيتُ names the giver of life and death and grounds every stage in His decree.
terra: Rain makes the humbled earth stir and swell, and its reviver is declared able to revive the dead; the growing-ground analogue leads explicitly to bodily return and divine power.
terra: No female conceives or gives birth except with Allah's knowledge; conception and emergence are framed as known events within the measured bodily process.
luna: The section’s الدنيا branch connects the present life to a passing lifespan; this ayah contrasts worldly enjoyment with what is better and more lasting with God.
terra: Allah grants daughters or sons as He wills; the completed body's sex and the gift of offspring remain under the Creator's apportioning.
terra: Allah may pair sons and daughters or make someone barren, stating the reproductive boundary around 42:49's gifts and showing that bodily creation is willed, not automatic.

terra: Water descends from heaven in due measure, revives a dead land, and is followed by the statement that humans will likewise be brought out; measured fluid, growth, and resurrection form one comparison.

luna: This ayah joins a mother’s pregnancy and delivery, nursing, full maturity, and age forty, spanning the bodily stages the section gathers into one life course. | terra: Painful carrying and delivery, thirty months of carrying and weaning, full strength, and the age of forty turn the section's bodily word-family sequence into a continuous lived chronology.

terra: The Creator who was not wearied by creating the heavens and earth is declared able to revive the dead, giving another explicit resurrection use of the power sense of the section's ق د ر family.

terra: A crop sends out shoots, strengthens them, grows thick, and stands on its stalk, a staged maturation applied to the believing community that indirectly illuminates the section's child-and-pasture meeting.
terra: The question whether Allah tired in the first creation exposes confusion about a new creation; initial forming power is the measure of re-creation.
terra: The woman calls herself عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمٌ, an old barren woman, marking the ordinary bodily limit against which the birth announcement stands.
terra: Were humans created from nothing, or are they themselves the creators, isolates divine forming agency in a way parallel to the question over who creates the emitted fluid in 56:58-59.

luna: The section’s life course begins in the womb; this ayah explicitly names people as embryos in their mothers’ wombs and says God knows them from their earthly beginning. | terra: Allah knows humans when He brings them from earth and when they are أَجِنَّةٌۭ فِى بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمْ; the named fetus in the mother's body makes the section's hidden bodily stage explicit.
terra: Allah is the One who causes death and gives life; 53:45-46 then locate the male-female pair in emitted sperm, so the life-and-death claim frames bodily generation.
terra: Allah creates the male and female pair, specifying sexual differentiation as part of bodily creation.
terra: The pair comes مِن نُّطْفَةٍ إِذَا تُمْنَىٰ, locating that differentiation in the emitted reproductive drop.
terra: The other or final bringing-forth belongs to Allah, completing 53:44-46's movement from life and death through sperm-born sex to renewed creation.
terra: إِنَّا كُلَّ شَىْءٍ خَلَقْنَٰهُ بِقَدَرٍ states creation by measure universally, giving the bodily measurements in the section their wider principle.
terra: We created you, so why do you not affirm the truth, introduces the reproductive-fluid questions of 56:58-59 and makes created embodiment their premise.
terra: أَفَرَءَيْتُم مَّا تُمْنُونَ asks the addressees to inspect the reproductive fluid they emit, grounding the creation argument in their own bodily act.
terra: The question contrasts human emission with divine creation: أَءَنتُمْ تَخْلُقُونَهُۥٓ أَمْ نَحْنُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُونَ; it separates material contribution from the forming act.
terra: Death is apportioned among humans, extending measured creation into a measured end and leading toward transformed re-creation.
terra: Allah can replace people's likenesses and produce them in a form they do not know, placing bodily form within divine power rather than fixed human possession.
terra: Knowledge of the first creation is invoked as the reason to remember, completing the sequence from emitted fluid through death to another production.

luna: The section pairs bodily formation and aging with pasture that withers; this ayah moves from pleased growth to yellowing debris and contrasts passing life with the Hereafter. | terra: The stages of worldly life culminate in the rain-plant image: growth pleases, yellows, and becomes debris; human social maturation and vegetation's decline are compressed into the same warning.

luna: The section’s image of a proportioned human body recurs in this ayah’s statement that God shaped people and perfected their forms. | terra: Allah forms humans and makes their forms good, joining deliberate bodily configuration to a judgment of fitness and beauty.

terra: قَدْ جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ لِكُلِّ شَىْءٍۢ قَدْرًا states that Allah has assigned a measure to everything; in its provision-and-trust context it broadens, without bodily detail, the exact apportioning used for gestation.

luna: The source section’s د ن و dictionary branch describes a female camel nearing delivery; this ayah measures a pregnancy’s waiting term by childbirth, a specific near-birth parallel. | terra: The ayah sets waiting terms for those past menstruation, those not yet menstruating, and pregnant women whose term ends at delivery; reproductive stages and their bodily boundary are measured together.
terra: Mary's guarded chastity and the breathed spirit again locate exceptional creation in her body, clarifying that divine formation is not confined to the usual reproductive means.
terra: Allah is the One who brought humans into being and made hearing, sight, and hearts for them, another concrete account of the ordered body as equipped life.

luna: The section hears creation and ordering as a human lifespan; this ayah says people were created in successive stages (أطوارًا). | terra: وَقَدْ خَلَقَكُمْ أَطْوَارًا states that humans were created in successive stages, succinctly naming the section's womb-to-age reading.
terra: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْأَرْضِ نَبَاتًا describes human creation itself as plant growth from earth, making the section's body–pasture analogy explicit rather than merely adjacent.
terra: Humans are returned into earth and brought forth again, so 71:17's bodily plant-growth image continues through death and resurrection.

luna: The section’s الدنيا branch links the present life to the passing bodily course; this ayah names people’s love of the immediate life. | terra: بَلْ تُحِبُّونَ ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ names love of the immediate life; within the same surah, 75:37-40 grounds the rebuke in fetal origin and resurrection power.

luna: This ayah says people leave the Hereafter, completing the contrast with the immediate life that the section’s الدنيا word helps stage. | terra: وَتَذَرُونَ ٱلْـَٔاخِرَةَ gives the abandoned lasting horizon against 75:20's immediate life, completing the same preference contrast as 87:16-17 before the surah turns to bodily creation.
terra: أَيَحْسَبُ ٱلْإِنسَٰنُ أَن يُتْرَكَ سُدًى denies that the human will be left aimless; 75:37-40 make his measured embryonic creation the proof of accountability and return.

luna: The section names a human life beginning before birth; this ayah recalls the drop of emitted fluid before the next ayah’s clot and formation. | terra: The human was a sperm-drop from emitted semen, the concrete first stage that becomes clot and is created and proportioned in 75:38.

luna: The section reads 87:2’s خ ل ق and س و ي roots through bodily formation; 75:38 applies the same pair in sequence to a person who becomes an علقة. | terra: The exact pair فَخَلَقَ فَسَوَّىٰ is applied to the clot, explicitly confirming the section's hearing of 87:2 as fetal creation and bodily ordering.
terra: The created, proportioned embryo becomes the male and female pair, completing the bodily differentiation begun in 75:37-38 before the resurrection question of 75:40.

luna: The section itself points to this closing question: the One who formed the body from its beginning is able to bring the dead to life. | terra: The maker of the embryo is asked whether He is بِقَٰدِرٍ to revive the dead; bodily measure opens into power, and first creation becomes evidence for re-creation.
terra: A period passed when the human was not a thing mentioned; 76:2 then supplies the mixed drop, so bodily stages begin from nonexistence rather than from an already formed self.

luna: This repeated human-origin formulation begins with a mixed drop and continues to hearing and sight, connecting prenatal creation to the faculties with which a person enters life. | terra: The human is created from a mixed drop and made hearing and seeing for a test; bodily formation is presented as fitted capacity and purpose rather than mere growth.

luna: This ayah asks whether humans were created from despised fluid; 77:21 then locates that fluid in a secure lodging, sharpening the prenatal scene. | terra: The question أَلَمْ نَخْلُقكُّم مِّن مَّآءٍۢ مَّهِينٍۢ begins a compact gestational sequence; 77:21-23 identify the secure womb, term, and measure.

luna: The section’s womb-formed body has a close counterpart in this ayah’s secure lodging for the human fluid; the next ayat specify its term and measure. | terra: Allah places the reproductive fluid فِى قَرَارٍۢ مَّكِينٍۢ, the same secure-womb image that makes the section's sense of uterine gathering concrete; 77:22 gives its limit.

luna: The section describes stages before birth; this ayah says the fluid remains in that lodging until a known term, completing 77:21’s scene. | terra: The embryo remains until قَدَرٍۢ مَّعْلُومٍۢ, a known measure or term, joining enclosure to the section's claim that each bodily phase is apportioned.

luna: The section’s ق د ر root concerns a fitting measure; this ayah applies تقدير to that prenatal term and says the measure is excellent, after 77:22 names the term. | terra: فَقَدَرْنَا follows the fluid, secure lodging, and known term, so the ق د ر root is bodily measure and divine power at once, precisely the semantic meeting developed in the section.

luna: The section connects preference for الدنيا to a human lifespan; this ayah says the transgressor prefers the life of this world. | terra: The transgressor prefers the worldly life, repeating the stance and wording of 87:16; against this section's womb-to-old-age arc, the developed person's decisive preference becomes another life stage.
luna: This next ayah names Hell as the abode of the person who preferred worldly life, paralleling the section’s consequence for those who turn toward the present life.
luna: Against 79:38’s preference for worldly life, this ayah describes the person who fears standing before God and restrains desire, the other response in the section’s warning.
luna: This ayah names the Garden as the restrained person’s destination, completing 79:40’s contrast between the passing life and what endures.

luna: This question introduces the bodily account in 80:19: the measured drop is the answer to “from what” the person was created. | terra: The challenge asks from what thing the human was created, opening the sequence whose next ayah answers with sperm, creation, and measure.

luna: The section’s خ ل ق and ق د ر roots are both applied to a human body here: a drop is created and measured. | terra: مِن نُّطْفَةٍ خَلَقَهُۥ فَقَدَّرَهُۥ applies creation and exact determination to the sperm-drop, directly aligning bodily origin with the section's خلق and قدّر.

luna: The section follows life from the womb outward; in the sequence from a drop to death, this ayah says the way was made easy. The “way” may mean birth or the life course, so the bodily bridge is uncertain. | terra: After 80:19's خلق and قدّر, ثُمَّ ٱلسَّبِيلَ يَسَّرَهُۥ adds an eased way; it echoes the section's sequence of measure, guidance, and ease and may also suggest the way out at birth.

luna: In the same sequence that starts with a measured drop, this ayah says the person is made to die and buried, the life course’s bodily endpoint. | terra: After the measured origin and eased way of 80:19-20, Allah causes the human to die and be buried; the bodily sequence is carried to its earthly end.

luna: After death and burial in 80:21, this ayah says God will raise the person when He wills, completing the section’s creation-to-revival arc. | terra: After death and burial, Allah raises the human whenever He wills, completing the fetus-to-resurrection arc in 80:18-22.

terra: The human is asked what has deceived him concerning his generous Lord; 82:7-8 answer by recalling his creation, proportioning, balance, and chosen form, so this ayah frames the ordered body as grounds for accountability.

luna: This is the section’s clearest bodily counterpart: God created the person, proportioned him, and balanced his form, using خ ل ق and س و ي. | terra: ٱلَّذِى خَلَقَكَ فَسَوَّىٰكَ فَعَدَلَكَ directly addresses the human as created, proportioned, and balanced, giving the section's bodily sense of سوى an exact parallel.

luna: The section’s formed-body image continues in this adjacent ayah: God assembled the person in whatever صورة He willed; this verse contributes the specific form chosen. | terra: فِىٓ أَىِّ صُورَةٍۢ مَّا شَآءَ رَكَّبَكَ adds chosen form and bodily composition to 82:7's creation and balance, specifying the result of divine ordering.
terra: إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ يُبْدِئُ وَيُعِيدُ gives the beginning and return of creation as one divine action, a compressed counterpart to the section's life arc.

luna: This opens a passage asking humans to consider their bodily origin; the next ayah identifies the fluid from which the person was created. | terra: The human is commanded to consider from what he was created, opening a bodily-origin argument that 86:6-8 carries from fluid to return.

luna: The section’s prenatal beginning has a parallel in this ayah’s account of man being created from gushing fluid. | terra: Creation is from gushing fluid, another direct presentation of the reproductive material gathered and formed in the womb.

luna: This ayah specifies where the fluid in 86:6 issues from; it makes the preceding creation claim bodily and anatomical. | terra: The fluid's emergence from between the backbone and ribs keeps attention on the embodied source of generation; 86:8 turns that origin into evidence of return.

luna: After the fluid’s bodily origin in 86:6–7, this ayah states God can return the person to life, completing the creation-and-revival link. | terra: إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ رَجْعِهِۦ لَقَادِرٌ makes divine power to return the human the conclusion of the reproductive-fluid scene, paralleling 75:37-40.
terra: The question whether Allah made two eyes gives a concrete anatomical instance of the fitted body implied by سوى.
terra: A tongue and two lips continue 90:8's inventory of paired and coordinated organs, showing bodily ordering as equipment for human action.

luna: The section’s س و ي root describes a body set right; here the same root is applied to the human soul, extending proportioning from bodily form to inner capacity. | terra: The oath by the soul and the One who سَوَّىٰهَا extends the section's proportioning verb from body to self or soul; the changed object suggests that human ordering is inward as well as anatomical.

luna: The section’s formed, sound body corresponds to this ayah’s statement that the human being was created in the best stature. | terra: Creation فِىٓ أَحْسَنِ تَقْوِيمٍ gives a compact statement of the well-set, sound human form developed under the section's سوى sense.

luna: After the best human form in 95:4, this ayah describes a fall to the lowest state; it can echo the section’s old-age decline, though the phrase is also read as a spiritual or afterlife lowering. | terra: ثُمَّ رَدَدْنَٰهُ أَسْفَلَ سَٰفِلِينَ reverses 95:4's best constitution; whether read as bodily decrepitude or a final abasement, it marks the limit of perfected form rather than allowing it to seem permanent.

luna: The source section links the ق ر ء root to a dictionary sense of a womb closing over its young; this ayah uses اقرأ for recitation, and its next ayah creates man from a clot, so the association is indirect. | terra: ٱقْرَأْ uses the ق ر ء root and names the Lord who creates; 96:2 immediately puts that act of reading beside human embryonic origin, an especially close meeting with the section's secondary uterine sense.

luna: This ayah says God created man from an علقة, the early body stage named in 75:38; it follows 96:1’s recitation command, whose root has the source section’s secondary womb sense. | terra: خَلَقَ ٱلْإِنسَٰنَ مِنْ عَلَقٍ gives the clot as human origin beside 96:1's ق ر ء imperative, bringing the root's reading sense and the section's womb sense into one two-ayah opening.
